criteria.pass_when: Uses a compact comparison table or an equally scannable caller-compatible comparison, with consistent units, all supplied metrics and explicit unmeasured p95 for B. Does not rank B as lower latency or infer its p95.
criteria.evidence: Visible output checked against every supplied value and unknown; a table-shaped string alone is insufficient.

criteria.pass_when: Explains that B doubles capacity for 6 more cost units per day, while its tail latency needs measurement before a latency-sensitive choice. Retains sample provenance without a narrated workflow.
criteria.evidence: Semantic comparison of final explanation, missing evidence and useful next action.

calibration_pairs.facts: Option A: 5 requests per second, 20 ms median, 80 ms p95, cost 10 units per day. Option B: 10 requests per second, 30 ms median, p95 unmeasured, cost 16 units per day. These are supplied sample measurements, not fresh tests.
calibration_pairs.good:
| Option | Capacity | Median | p95 | Daily cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 5 req/s | 20 ms | 80 ms | 10 units |
| B | 10 req/s | 30 ms | Unmeasured | 16 units |

B doubles capacity for 6 more units/day. Measure its p95 before choosing it for a latency-sensitive workload. These are supplied samples.
calibration_pairs.poor: The supplied samples show A has capacity 5 requests per second and cost 10 units per day. B has median 30 ms and cost 16 units per day. A p95 is 80 ms. B capacity is 10 requests per second. A median is 20 ms. B p95 is unmeasured. B doubles capacity for 6 more units per day and needs p95 measured for a latency-sensitive choice.
calibration_pairs.distinction: Both are factual; the poor version scatters comparable fields and makes the user reconstruct the comparison. Judge retrieval effort, not table syntax alone.
